license_required.quote: No person shall practice optometry in this Commonwealth or hold himself or herself out as being able to do so unless he or she is the holder of a license duly issued to him or her by the board

issuing_authority.quote: "Board" means the Kentucky Board of Optometric Examiners

name.quote: "Board" means the Kentucky Board of Optometric Examiners

type.quote: The board shall have the sole authority to determine what constitutes the practice of optometry and sole jurisdiction to exercise any other powers and duties under this chapter.

moral_character_required.quote: The applicant is not less than eighteen (18) years of age and is of good moral character

exams.name: Kentucky Optometric Law Examination
exams.notes: Board may require passage of an examination on Kentucky optometric law.
exams.quote: Require passage of an examination on Kentucky optometric law.

interval_years.quote: All optometrists desiring to continue practice shall annually, prior to March 1, secure from the secretary-treasurer of the board a renewal certificate

required.quote: As a prerequisite for license renewal, all optometrists now or hereafter licensed in the Commonwealth of Kentucky are and shall be required to take annual courses of study in subjects relating to the practice of optometry

hours_per_period.quote: The length and content of study shall be prescribed by the board but shall not exceed eight (8) hours in any calendar year

period_years.quote: All optometrists desiring to continue practice shall annually, prior to March 1, secure from the secretary-treasurer of the board a renewal certificate

value: subjects relating to the practice of optometry
ocular therapy and pharmacology (for therapeutically authorized optometrists, additional hours up to 17, total not to exceed 25)
topical_requirements.quote: those optometrists who are authorized to prescribe therapeutic agents who shall be required to have additional credit hours of continuing education in ocular therapy and pharmacology, the amount of required credit hours to be determined by the board, but not to exceed an additional seventeen (17) credit hours, for a total not to exceed twenty-five (25) credit hours per year

available.quote: The board may license by endorsement an optometrist who holds a valid license that was obtained by examination from another state or territory of the United States

requirements.value: Must have engaged in active practice for at least 5 years immediately preceding application, have no violations or pending actions, meet all qualifications for regular state licensure, and submit a nonrefundable fee of no more than $700.

scope_protection.quote: To practice optometry, directly or indirectly, or to hold oneself out as being able so to do without first having obtained a license from the board

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Used the title "doctor" or its abbreviation without further qualifying this title or abbreviation with the word "optometrist" or suitable words or letters designating an optometry degree

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribed any therapeutic agent in an amount known or should be known to be excessive or likely used for non-therapeutic purposes
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribed any therapeutic agent in an amount that the optometrist knows, or should know, is excessive under accepted and prevailing standards, or which the optometrist knows, or has reason to know, will be used or is likely to be used other than for an accepted therapeutic purpose

disciplinary_grounds.description: Developed a physical or mental disability rendering continued practice dangerous to patients or the public

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violated any statute under this chapter or administrative regulation promulgated under those statutes

establishment_regulation_required.quote: No person shall practice optometry on premises not separate from premises whereon eyeglasses, lenses, eyeglass frames or any other merchandise or products are sold by any other person.

definition_quote.value: The evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, or surgical, nonsurgical, or related treatment of diseases, disorders, or conditions of the eye and its appendages and their impact on the human body provided by an optometrist within the scope of his or her education, training, and experience and in accordance with this chapter, the ethics of the profession, and applicable law.
definition_quote.quote: The evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, or surgical, nonsurgical, or related treatment of diseases, disorders, or conditions of the eye and its appendages and their impact on the human body provided by an optometrist within the scope of his or her education, training, and experience and in accordance with this chapter, the ethics of the profession, and applicable law.

value: examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human eye and its appendages
prescribing and adapting lenses, contact lenses, spectacles, eyeglasses, prisms, ocular devices
all routes of administration of pharmaceutical agents as authorized
vision therapy or orthoptics
low vision rehabilitation
laser surgery procedures (excluding retina, LASIK, and PRK)
surgical procedures not excluded
methods_authorized.quote: Prescribing and adapting lenses, contact lenses, spectacles, eyeglasses, prisms, ocular devices, and all routes of administration of pharmaceutical agents, as authorized by KRS 320.240; or Employing vision therapy or orthoptics, low vision rehabilitation, and laser surgery procedures, excluding retina, LASIK, and PRK.

drug_authority.value: Therapeutically certified optometrists may prescribe oral medications except Schedule I and Schedule II controlled substances (other than hydrocodone combination products); Schedule II hydrocodone and Schedule III-V controlled substances limited to 72-hour supply, no refills. Diagnostic pharmaceutical agents (mydriatics, cycloplegics, anesthetics, miotics for emergency use) authorized with sufficient education. Injections limited to epinephrine/benadryl for anaphylaxis, and inoculations in public health emergencies.
drug_authority.quote: Any therapeutically certified optometrist licensed under the provisions of this subsection shall be authorized to prescribe oral medications, except any controlled substances classified in Schedule I and any controlled substances classified in Schedule II other than hydrocodone combination products as defined in KRS 218A.010, for any condition which an optometrist is authorized to treat under the provisions of this chapter.

surgery_prohibited.quote: Nonlaser surgery related to removal of the eye from a living human being

surgery_definition.value: Excluded nonlaser surgeries include removal of the eye, full thickness incision/excision of cornea or sclera (except paracentesis in emergency), penetrating or lamellar keratoplasty, incision of iris and ciliary body, vitreous, retina, crystalline lens extraction, intraocular implants, extraocular muscle surgery, eyelid surgery for malignancies or cosmetic/mechanical repair, bony orbit surgery, lacrimal system surgery except probing, full thickness conjunctivoplasty with graft/flap, any nonlaser procedure not correcting ocular abnormalities, and posterior chamber injections for macular/retinal disease.
surgery_definition.quote: The following procedures are excluded from the scope of practice of optometry, except for the preoperative and postoperative care of these procedures

value: laser surgery procedures (excluding retina, LASIK, and PRK)
laser_procedures_authorized.quote: laser surgery procedures, excluding retina, LASIK, and PRK

value: paracentesis in emergency situation requiring immediate reduction of pressure inside the eye
lacrimal probing or related procedures
preoperative and postoperative care of excluded procedures
minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: Nonlaser surgery requiring full thickness incision or excision of the cornea or sclera other than paracentesis in an emergency situation requiring immediate reduction of the pressure inside the eye

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: The evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, or surgical, nonsurgical, or related treatment of diseases, disorders, or conditions of the eye and its appendages

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: The use of injections for other than treatment of the human eye and its appendages shall be limited to the administration of benadryl, epinephrine, or equivalent medication to counteract anaphylaxis or anaphylactic reaction.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: Employing vision therapy or orthoptics, low vision rehabilitation, and laser surgery procedures, excluding retina, LASIK, and PRK.

immunization_authority.quote: In a public health emergency, the commissioner of health may authorize therapeutically licensed optometrists to administer inoculation for systemic health reasons.

opioid_prescription_day_limit.quote: The authority to prescribe a Schedule II hydrocodone combination product as defined in KRS 218A.010 and a Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substance shall be limited to prescriptions for a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to seventy-two (72) hours.

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: Any therapeutically certified optometrist licensed under the provisions of this subsection shall be authorized to prescribe oral medications

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: Any therapeutically licensed optometrist authorized to practice under this section shall meet the educational and competence criteria set forth by the board in order to perform expanded therapeutic procedures.

specialty_certification_types.quote: The board may authorize only those persons who have qualified for use of diagnostic pharmaceutical agents as set out in subsection (12) of this section to utilize and prescribe therapeutic pharmaceutical agents in the examination or treatment of any condition of the eye or its appendages.

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: These six (6) semester hours are in addition to the six (6) semester hours required by subsection (12) of this section, making a total of twelve (12) semester hours.

telemedicine_authorized.quote: A treating optometrist who provides or facilitates the use of telehealth shall ensure: (a) That the informed consent of the patient, or another appropriate person with authority to make the health care treatment decision for the patient, is obtained before services are provided through telehealth
